newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares rise but trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares rise but trade quiet.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose slightly on Sunday in quiet trade dominated by two popular stocks that have issued global depository receipts (GDRs).
The Capital Market Authority overall index closed 0.61 points higher at 337.17 in below-average trade of 33 million pounds ($9.7 million).

"The market is picking up quite slowly but quite surely. It doesn't mean it has completely turned around but it will be ready once we reach September and funds are pushed into the market," said Ahmed el-Helw of Intercapital Brokerage.
Commercial International Bank (CIB), which closed 0.67 pounds higher, was the day's most active stock after shares worth 4.5 million pounds changed hands.
The bank's profit for the first six months of calender 1997, its financial year, rose to 133.768 million pounds from 122.365 million in the same year ago period.
CIB was Egypt's first GDR offering. Stock in the bank was sold through GDRs listed on the London exchange in July 1996.
Suez Cement, part of which was sold through a GDR offering in October 1996, also did well on Sunday's market.
The cement stock closed 0.4 pounds higher at 63.91 after shares worth 3.5 million pounds were traded.
Suez Cement profits for the first half of calender 1997, the firm's financial year, rose to 158.5 million pounds from 151 million in the same period a year ago.
"A lot of the trade is arbitrage from the GDRs to the local market," Helw said.
Another cement favourite, Amriyah Cement, traded in shares worth 3.3 million pounds and closed 0.3 pounds higher at 80.14.

The government al-Ahram newspaper last week quoted Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif as saying the ministerial committee on privatisation had approved the sale of 20 percent of the holding company's stake in Amriyah through the bourse and 28 percent via GDRs to relinquish its stake in the cement firm.
"Amriyah is trading at a low price so you can call it investor friendly," Helw said.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 460.47 points from 454.02 points on Thursday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 249.71 from 250.78.
Of the 83 shares traded, 34 rose, 37 ended lower and 12 remained unchanged.
